{{Quote|The Signatories of Waymancy had to be stopped. Some of their number believed in fanaticism, some believed in territorial cleansing, some believed in nothing at all beyond the cold logic of machinery. But the wholesale murder of settlers and their families? That could only be practiced by those who believed in evil.|Supreme Chancellor Nagratha|<ref name="Author's Cut" />}}
The '''Signatories of Waymancy''' were a faction that fought against the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] in the [[Waymancy Storm]] of [[7811 BBY]]. The conflict ignited following the first contact between the Republic and [[Warship/Legends|warships]] of the [[Waymancy Hollow]] region, inside of which the [[Sisters of the Machinesmith]] had studied and improved Republic technology. Believing in fanaticism and territorial cleansing and possessing technological superiority over their enemy, the Signatories of Waymancy targeted both the Republic's military assets and its civilian settlers in the [[Northern Dependencies/Legends|Northern Dependencies]], inflicting large casualties. Eventually, however, the Republic managed to turn the tide of the conflict in its favor and ultimately emerge victorious over the Signatories' forces.

==Description==
{{Quote|For while we in the Republic possessed an unquenchable fighting spirit, our enemy had a cold, automated edge. After studying our technology for a thousand years inside the Waymancy Hollow, the Sisters of the Machinesmith had improved on our designs in nearly every way.|Supreme Chancellor Nagratha|<ref name="Author's Cut" />}}
[[File:Waymancy-EGTW.png|thumb|right|300px|The Signatories of Waymancy shared their name with the Waymancy system.]]
The Signatories of Waymancy were a faction<ref name="Author's Cut" /> that shared their name with the [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim's]] [[Waymancy system/Legends|Waymancy system]],<ref name="EAOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}}</ref> the [[Waymancy Hollow]] region, and the object known as the [[Waymancy bridal seat]]. The forces allied with the Signatories of Waymancy included the [[Fleet/Legends|armadas]] of the [[Wives of Tingrippa]], the [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] [[Army/Legends|army]] of [[Whirl-Point-Six]], a [[Neshtabine]] nest on the celestial body [[Tantara]], and at least one raider from<ref name="Author's Cut" /> the [[Planet/Legends|world]] [[Doshan]]<ref name="IH">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''</ref> and one thug from<ref name="Author's Cut" /> the planet [[Muzara]].<ref name="TotJC">''[[Tales of the Jedi Companion]]''</ref>

According to a later description by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic's]] [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Nagratha]], the beliefs of the constituent members of the Signatories included fanaticism, territorial cleansing, and the "cold logic of machinery." Although, during the conflict known as the [[Waymancy Storm]], the [[Republic Military/Legends|Republic armed forces]] exhibited great determination in their fight against the Signatories of Waymancy and outnumbered those of the Signatories a hundred to one, the latter possessed a significant edge due to technological superiority, including [[Warship/Legends|warships]] that could fly farther and faster than those used by the Republic and [[Deflector shield/Legends|energy shields]] and [[Pulse-wave blaster|pulse-wave]] [[Weapon/Legends|weaponry]]&mdash;both [[Starship/Legends|starship]]-mounted and personal-scale&mdash;that outclassed the Republic's military equipment.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

==History==
{{Quote|Though we outnumbered our enemies a hundred to one, the frightful killing machines wielded by tyrants absent of conscience inflicted terrible losses in our ranks.|Supreme Chancellor Nagratha|<ref name="Author's Cut" />}}
Inside the Waymancy Hollow, the group known as the [[Sisters of the Machinesmith]] studied and improved upon the Galactic Republic's technology for a [[Millennium/Legends|millennium]] leading up to [[7811 BBY]].<ref name="Author's Cut" /> That [[Standard year/Legends|year]], the Republic established disastrous first contact with warships associated with the Waymancy Hollow. The encounter led to the Waymancy Storm,<ref name="EGTW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> which was waged between the Republic and the Signatories of Waymancy in several [[Star system/Legends|star systems]]<ref name="Author's Cut" /> in the [[Northern Dependencies/Legends|Northern Dependencies]] portion of the Inner Rim and the [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansion Region]].<ref name="Systems">{{SW|url=news/the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-part-4-the-rise-of-the-republic-needs-author-entry|series=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|text=Part 4: The Rise of the Republic}} notes several astronomical objects at which battles and other events of the [[Waymancy Storm]] occurred. ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' places all of the corresponding [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] in an area of [[Realspace/Legends|space]] ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' identifies as part of the [[Northern Dependencies/Legends|Northern Dependencies]] portion of the [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]] and the [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansion Region]].</ref>

[[File:NorthernDependencies-TEA.jpg|thumb|left|300px|The Waymancy Storm was fought in the Northern Dependencies between the Galactic Republic and the Signatories of Waymancy.]]
During the Waymancy Storm, the Signatories of Waymancy targeted both the Republic's armed forces and its civilian [[Colonist/Legends|colonists]], at one point causing the [[Death/Legends|deaths]] of ten million settlers on the astronomical object [[Upper Brightday]]. As the war progressed, the actions of the Signatories became progressively [[Blood/Legends|bloodier]]. Eventually, however, the Republic's fortune turned due to intense efforts by its [[Spy/Legends|spies]] and codebreakers at interpreting intercepted data and [[Scientist/Legends|scientific]] breakthroughs by technologists at a Republic [[Shipyard/Legends|shipyard]] on<ref name="Author's Cut" /> the planet<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> [[Axum]] who attempted to reverse-[[Engineer/Legends|engineer]] captured Waymancy technology.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

Armed with newly improved offensive and defensive capabilities, the Republic forces [[Rout on Tantara|routed]] the Tantara nest and [[Collapse of the Clowse Glowstack|destroyed]] the [[Clowse Glowstack]] on the celestial body [[Mittoblade/Legends|Mittoblade]], ultimately also reducing the Waymancy bridal seat to a [[hyperspace sinkhole]] and achieving overall victory in the conflict. At a speech delivered on the [[25th anniversary of Victory in the Waymancy Storm]] in [[7786 BBY]], Supreme Chancellor Nagratha gave a brief recount of the history of the conflict, in which they characterized the Signatories of Waymancy as "tyrants absent of conscience" and as a force of evil due to their killing of civilians. Nagratha also described the war as a "necessary" effort with the goal of stopping the Signatories' actions.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Signatories of Waymancy were originally meant to be mentioned in the [[2012]] reference book ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' by [[Jason Fry]] and [[Paul R. Urquhart]]; however, the section that would have mentioned the faction, authored by [[Daniel Wallace]], was cut before the book's release. The information regarding the Signatories of Waymancy was later released in [[2014]] as part of [[Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|''Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Author's Cut]], a series of articles published on the [[StarWars.com]] [[Star Wars Blog|Blog]] by Fry and<ref name="Author's Cut" /> [[Del Rey]] editor<ref name="Celestials">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-the-celestials|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Author's Cut — The Celestials|int=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut}}</ref> [[Erich Schoeneweiss]] containing various cut content from ''The Essential Guide to Warfare''.<ref name="Author's Cut" />
